title: I vibe coded a free old school style online RPG you play in the browser, as a solo dev with a full time job
author: QwaZz
selftext:
Hey all 👋



I'm Brenner. Crafted Realm is a free online RPG in the old school style that runs right in your browser, and I vibe code it as a passion project on top of my full time job. Without AI it simply wouldn't exist.



How it's built:

• The code is written with AI coding agents, mostly Claude Code with Codex on the side. I do the design, the world, the story and every call on what goes in

• Every model and animation is low poly and made in Blender

• A Node.js server runs the world on a tick, with a Three.js client in the browser

• Several agents work on separate parts of an update at once, and a main update doesn't ship until I've played it myself



It went live on 12 October and has had 21 updates since, most of them from player feedback. There are 19 skills, a team castle minigame, a player run market, bosses, and our first Halloween event running until 8 November. Controller support is coming in the next update.



Happy to answer anything about the workflow. And if you try it, I'd love to hear how the first ten minutes feel.



Play free (just a name and a password): [https://playcraftedrealm.com](https://playcraftedrealm.com)

Discord: [https://discord.gg/2wSMYr2Hra](https://discord.gg/2wSMYr2Hra)

replies.author: QwaZz
replies.body:
Thanks, really appreciate that! And yeah, agreed on the HUD. Giving it its own look is next on my list.



For the code I use Claude Code with Opus 5.5, which is honestly the GOAT right now.



For the art, the biggest thing was developing the style before building anything. I spent a lot of time early on just dialing in the overall feel: a cozy 3D world, low poly, old school, a little rough around the edges instead of polished. Once that was locked in, every new asset had something to match.



For individual assets my loop is pretty simple:



1. Ask ChatGPT's image generator for something like "low poly 3D old school style sword" and have it make 10 versions

2. Pull them into a little local page so I can compare them side by side

3. Pick the one I like best and save it

4. Upload that image into a folder for Claude code and have it build a Blender version and add it to the game



After that it's a lot of back and forth on the shape until it sits right next to everything else. The consistency mostly comes from always picking against the same style, not from some magic prompt.



Good luck with your game, I'd love to see it when it's out!
